But signed-index-trust-contract.v13 lands the unlabeled Codex signed-index-trust-contract.v12 SHOULD-FIX by editing a frozen-v12-speaker sentence in place rather than by opening its own honesty block. Character-level opcode diff isolates the whole v12 -> v13 change to one replace, '9' -> '10', at that position.
mustFix.whyThisIsAFinding: The entry is scoped by its own opening clause to the unlabeled Codex signed-index-trust-contract.v11 SHOULD-FIX, and its closing sentence names signed-index-trust-contract.v12 as the actor. Every sentence between them is therefore a statement about what signed-index-trust-contract.v12 did. As now written, the entry asserts that the v12 repair set the historical declaration to honestyRepairsFromV10. It did not; it set it to honestyRepairsFromV9, which is precisely why the frozen Codex signed-index-trust-contract.v12 review returned a SHOULD-FIX. signed-index-trust-contract.v13 has put words in a frozen predecessor's mouth and pinned the digest that refutes them in the same document. The alternative reading - that the sentence is signed-index-trust-contract.v13's own live declaration parked inside a v12-speaker entry - does not rescue it: it makes the entry mix a v12-speaker actor sentence with an unlabeled current-speaker claim, which is the speaker-currency defect this chain has policed since CLAUDE-V11-M1 and which honestyRepairsFromV11[0] names in its own bytes as 'v11-to-v12 speaker-currency leaves'. Either reading yields a defect.
mustFix.selfContradiction: The artifact states the correct remedy twice in its own bytes and then does the opposite. honestyRepairsFromV2[3]: 'correction recorded here, not by mutating honestyRepairsFromV1'. honestyRepairsFromV11[1] itself - the very entry rewritten: 'honestyRepairsFromV9 restored byte-for-byte from frozen signed-index-trust-contract.v10. v10-to-v11 statements remain in honestyRepairsFromV10.' That is the codified rule: a wrong statement in a predecessor's block is repaired by restoring the block and recording the correction in the current generation's block, never by editing the predecessor's words. signed-index-trust-contract.v13 edits the predecessor's words.
